editorial.dek: The Season in Review is live: LibertyBiberty's 87-point comeback, Love on MyBallz' suspiciously lucky 8-2, the Yinzers' summer fire sale, and nine awards nobody asked for.

stories.h: LibertyBiberty trail by 87.48, win by 32.18, and remind everyone who runs this league
stories.body: Carson City Yinzers led 135.48 to 48.0 after the early Sunday games in Week 10 and probably started drafting the group-chat message. Then Christian McCaffrey scored 46.3, Joe Burrow added 41.16 on Sunday night, and LibertyBiberty won 211.76 to 179.58. They're 8-2 with 148.77 more points than anybody else. The full Season in Review has everything that's happened through Week 10, and nobody is spared.

stories.h: Love on MyBallz keep winning; C-Money keep not winning
stories.body: Love on MyBallz beat ADUBB818 170.76 to 162.56 for their fourth straight win, because ADUBB818 are not allowed to have nice things. I Can’t Quit Tuten beat C-Money 168.86 to 130.38, C-Money's second straight loss, and moved to 6-4 alongside KittleMehThis, who beat AnnexationOfPR 163.12 to 115.06.

stories.h: The Donner Party eat Upper Deckers alive, 169.42 to 101.52
stories.body: The widest margin of Week 10, 67.9 points. Upper Deckers are 3-7 with the fewest points in the league and a highlight reel that would fit on a sticky note. Elsewhere, Diddys Oilers beat hopethisHurts 151.04 to 127.5, handing hopethisHurts their fourth straight loss. It continues to hurt.

recaps.h: LibertyBiberty are a cheat code, Love on MyBallz are lucky, and the Yinzers traded their whole team for picks

10.title: Season in Review
10.dek: Ten weeks in: LibertyBiberty are a cheat code, Love on MyBallz are 8-2 thanks to a schedule that clearly owes them money, Carson City Yinzers traded away their whole roster for picks and are acting surprised about 3-7, and AnnexationOfPR lost seven straight before deciding, out of nowhere, to beat the best team in the league. Pull up a chair. Nobody comes out of this clean.

stories.h: LibertyBiberty are not playing the same sport as the rest of you
stories.body: 8-2. 1,785.74 points, which is 148.77 more than second place, a gap you could park a Week 2 Love on MyBallz lineup in. Their all-play record, what they'd be if they played all 11 teams every week, is 88-22. Second best is C-Money at 69-41. They've had the week's top score three times and have won three games after trailing by 45 or more, including Week 10 from 87.48 down, which is less a comeback and more a hostage situation. Their two losses: Love on MyBallz in Week 1, and the 1-7 AnnexationOfPR in Week 9, which we'll get to, because it's the funniest thing that's happened all year.

stories.h: Love on MyBallz are 8-2 and should probably buy a lottery ticket
stories.body: Fifth in points scored. First in the standings. That math works because Love on MyBallz have had the fewest points scored against them in the league, 1,397.5, which means their opponents keep showing up like they're there to help. Their all-play record is 64-46, which is good, not 8-2 good. They won Week 2 with 110 points, the lowest winning score of the season, a number that loses to most of this league's benches. They've won four straight. Also, and this needs to be said: Bhayshul Tuten plays for Love on MyBallz. Not for I Can’t Quit Tuten. The team named after him doesn't have him. Somebody quit Tuten after all.

stories.h: Carson City Yinzers held a fire sale and are now living in the ashes
stories.body: This summer the Yinzers sent Ashton Jeanty to hopethisHurts for three first-round picks and Malik Nabers to I Can’t Quit Tuten for two firsts and a third, then flipped one of those firsts to C-Money for Rome Odunze, like a guy who sells his car and buys a bike with the money. They are 3-7. They've lost twice after leading by 45-plus. Their 179.58 in Week 10 is the highest losing score of the season. They've left 390.3 points on the bench, second most in the league. The good news, and there is some: the site's dynasty values have them first in the league at 75,983. The bad news: their starting lineup ranks tenth, and you can't start a 2028 first.

stories.h: hopethisHurts bought Jeanty, hit the season high, and then it did, in fact, hurt
stories.body: Week 1: 237.02 points, the best score anyone has put up all year, with Jeanty dropping 32.7 in his debut. Life was good. They were 4-2 after Week 6. They've lost four straight since, including the season's biggest beatdown, 190.32 to 103.04 against ADUBB818. They've left 422.9 points on the bench, the most in the league, including Devin Lloyd's 56.9 in Week 2. That's the highest score by any player this season, and it happened on the bench, which is like hitting a hole-in-one at the driving range. Bonus pain: the 2027 first they sent to the Yinzers now belongs to C-Money, who would like to thank them for every loss. Meanwhile I Can’t Quit Tuten, the Nabers buyers, are 6-4 despite starting seven players who scored zero, the most in the league. Seven. They're not setting lineups, they're filling out a raffle.

stories.h: ADUBB818 have the second-most points in the league and a 4-6 record, which is legally a crime
stories.body: 1,636.97 points, second only to LibertyBiberty. A 67-43 all-play record, third best. Tied for seventh in the standings, which is insane. They lost five straight from Week 2 to Week 6 while scoring like a contender, won three straight, then lost Week 10 to Love on MyBallz (of course) by 8.2 with T.J. Hockenson putting up a zero in the lineup. Their best lineup would've won. If this league paid out on points, ADUBB818 would be shopping for boats. It pays out on wins. Sorry.

stories.h: Everyone else: C-Money stall, Diddys Oilers fall off a cliff, and the basement has two tenants
stories.body: C-Money started 7-1 riding Jaxon Smith-Njigba, the top-scoring starter in the league at 264.7, then lost back-to-back to Love on MyBallz and I Can’t Quit Tuten, which is the kind of slump that only feels like a slump. KittleMehThis are 6-4 with two straight wins and are quietly hanging around like a guy at the bar who hasn't ordered yet. Diddys Oilers traded their 2027 first and a 2028 second to Upper Deckers for Davante Adams and Ollie Gordon II during Week 5, won that week to go 4-1, then lost four straight like the trade came with a curse. They're 5-5. Upper Deckers own that pick, plus the fewest points in the league (1,275.41), a 23-87 all-play record, and the only sub-100 score of the season. And AnnexationOfPR started 0-7, have had the most points dropped on them (1,677.98), and then beat Diddys Oilers and LibertyBiberty in back-to-back weeks for reasons science can't explain.

games.h: hopethisHurts drop 237.02, the season high, and Jeanty earns his three firsts in one afternoon
t: A couple of weeks after handing Carson City Yinzers three first-round picks for Ashton Jeanty, hopethisHurts put him straight in the lineup and he scored 32.7, which is the fantasy football equivalent of the new guy at work fixing the printer on day one. Derrick Henry added 35.3, Jalen Hurts 30.72, and the late Sunday window alone took them from 86.4 to 214.82. The final, 237.02, is still the highest score in the league ten weeks later.

And they left Bryce Young's 38.44 on the bench. Their best lineup was 251.94. Greedy. AnnexationOfPR scored 176.1, the third-best total of Week 1 and the second-highest losing score of the season, and lost by 60.92. It was the first of seven straight losses, so get comfortable with that name in this section.
games.v: Peak hopethisHurts. Enjoy the photo, because it's all downhill from here.

games.h: Love on MyBallz win with 110 points, and both managers should be ashamed
t: This game was two people trying to lose and only one of them being good at it. AnnexationOfPR started Jaxson Dart at quarterback. He scored 0.8. Bo Nix scored 17.12 on the bench. Love on MyBallz started Colston Loveland (1.3) and benched Tyler Shough (24.38) and Jake Ferguson (20.3), leaving 54.58 points on the pine. Somebody check on both of these guys.

It came down to Monday night, where Isaiah Likely's 8.3 beat Darnell Mooney's 6.8, and Love on MyBallz won 110 to 107.5. That's the lowest winning score of the season. AnnexationOfPR's best lineup would've scored 149.12 and won by 39.
games.v: Both teams set terrible lineups. Love on MyBallz got away with it. This will happen again. It will keep happening.

games.h: I Can’t Quit Tuten put up 229.03 while the two-first-round-pick guy naps
t: Bijan Robinson scored 35.3 on Thursday night and the late Sunday window piled on another 109.88: Brock Purdy 39.28, Juwan Johnson 28.8, and Nakobe Dean 26.6 from the linebacker spot. That's 229.03, the second-highest score of the season.

Malik Nabers, bought from the Yinzers for two firsts and a third, contributed 7.6. Didn't matter. Nobody needed him. Not a great sign for a guy who cost two firsts, but a great sign for the team. I Can’t Quit Tuten got their first win after an 0-2 start. AnnexationOfPR went to 0-3 and started looking up how to get out of a dynasty league.
games.v: The start of a four-game win streak for Tuten. AnnexationOfPR still at zero.

games.h: The Donner Party come back from 51.16 down, mostly because AnnexationOfPR ran out of players
t: By the end of the late Sunday games, AnnexationOfPR were finished: every starter had played, 150.06 points, done. The Donner Party had 98.9 and a Sunday night prayer. Jared Goff (22.48) and Jack Campbell (17.3) cut it to 11.38, then Xavier Watts scored 13.65 on Monday night and The Donner Party won 152.33 to 150.06. AnnexationOfPR watched the whole thing happen with nothing left to play, like being forced to watch your own robbery on a security camera.

To be clear, The Donner Party nearly blew it on Sunday morning by starting Ladd McConkey (0.0) while Nico Collins scored 30.8 on the bench. They won anyway. First win of the year. AnnexationOfPR dropped to 0-4, with losses by 60.92, 2.5, 84.49 and now 2.27. They're losing big, they're losing small, they're losing every way there is.
games.v: Monday night saved The Donner Party from Sunday morning The Donner Party.

games.h: LibertyBiberty erase a 56-point hole and ruin C-Money's perfect season
t: C-Money came in 4-0 and led 120.82 to 64.8 after the early games, behind 36.8 from Jaylen Warren. Then LibertyBiberty's late window showed up: Jahmyr Gibbs 37.7, Fred Warner 18, Christian McCaffrey 17.3, and just like that it was 180.2 and over. C-Money finished at 164.22.

C-Money will want to talk about CeeDee Lamb scoring 2.9. They will not want to talk about Malik Willis scoring 22.88 on their bench while Kirk Cousins put up 15.72 at quarterback. Their best lineup, 187.38, would have won. They benched the guy who would've kept them undefeated. Great stuff.
games.v: Comeback number one of three for LibertyBiberty. C-Money's 4-0 start ends with a benching they'd rather forget.

games.h: Upper Deckers score 98.3, the only time all season anyone has failed to reach 100
t: Upper Deckers started Kaleb Johnson, who scored -0.2, meaning he actively took points away. They also started Josh Cameron (0.0) and Mark Andrews (1.4). After the early games they had 81.5 and Carson City Yinzers had 164.44. Trevor Lawrence scored 36.34 for the Yinzers, who won 177.74 to 98.3.

The Yinzers did it with C.J. Stroud (29.98) and Michael Penix Jr. (29.1) both on the bench, so they could've scored even more if they'd felt like it. Upper Deckers' best possible lineup was 136.3, which also loses. There was no saving this. This was a team-wide power outage.
games.v: No lineup on Earth saves this week. Upper Deckers just had to sit there and take it.

games.h: Carson City Yinzers lead by 45.92, stop scoring, and lose by 33
t: The Yinzers led 119.92 to 74.0 after the early games, with Luther Burden III scoring 23.7 before Sunday even started. Then they scored 19.3 points for the rest of the weekend. Total. C-Money got 31.3 from Jaxon Smith-Njigba on Sunday night and 24.4 from CeeDee Lamb on Monday and won 172.4 to 139.22.

Meanwhile, sitting on the Yinzers' bench: KC Concepcion Jr. (23.2) and Caleb Douglas (21). Their best lineup was 188.92. Days later they traded Douglas and Omar Cooper Jr. to Diddys Oilers for Zach Charbonnet and a 2029 third. So the Yinzers did trade the guy off their bench. Just not before the game it would've mattered in.
games.v: C-Money go to 6-1. The Yinzers learn that a 45-point lead is more of a suggestion. They'll learn it again in Week 10.

t: After seven straight losses, it finally happened. AnnexationOfPR beat Diddys Oilers 164.88 to 142.26. Puka Nacua scored 25, Bo Nix 23.28, and D'Andre Swift put it away with 27.9 on Monday night. Somebody get that man a Gatorade bath.

Diddys Oilers made it easy. They started Omar Cooper Jr. in his first week after the trade with the Yinzers, and he scored 0.0. A fresh, brand-new zero. Alex Anzalone scored 31.8 on their bench. Diddys' best lineup, 167.66, would have won. That's three straight losses for Diddys, and the first time all year that losing to AnnexationOfPR was an option.
games.v: One down for AnnexationOfPR. Their reward: next week, the best team in the league.

games.h: The 1-7 team beats the 7-1 team, and nobody can explain it
t: AnnexationOfPR led the entire weekend by single digits and won 168.18 to 164.44, snapping LibertyBiberty's seven-game win streak. Puka Nacua scored 36.5 and Caleb Downs added 24.1 from the DB spot. LibertyBiberty got 35.54 from Joe Burrow and then 3.2 from Jaylen Waddle and 3.7 from Devaughn Vele, which is what happens when you start wide receivers you found in a couch cushion.

LibertyBiberty also left Daiyan Henley (26.4) and Dak Prescott (23.5) on the bench. Their best lineup was 199.94. And in the same week, ADUBB818 beat hopethisHurts 190.32 to 103.04, the biggest beatdown of the season, so Week 9 was a bad week to be the favorite and a worse week to be hopethisHurts.
games.v: The only loss LibertyBiberty have taken since Week 1, and it came from the team that couldn't beat anybody. Fantasy football, baby.

games.h: LibertyBiberty trail by 87.48, then win by 32.18, because of course they do
t: After the early Sunday games, Carson City Yinzers led 135.48 to 48.0. Chuba Hubbard had 34.2, Trevor Lawrence had 33.78, and for about three hours the Yinzers had every reason to believe. LibertyBiberty had Jahmyr Gibbs' 44.2 in the bank and a lot of players still to go. Christian McCaffrey dropped 46.3 in the late window. Joe Burrow dropped 41.16 on Sunday night. Final: 211.76 to 179.58. That 87.48 lead didn't just disappear; it got turned into a 32-point loss.

The Yinzers' 179.58 is the highest losing score of the season, which is a stat you only get to own if your week goes exactly this badly. And the cherry on top: LibertyBiberty had Dak Prescott on the bench scoring 45.42, more than Burrow did. They left 45 points on the bench and still won by 32. Some teams are just built different. Most of you are built like the Yinzers' Week 10 lineup after 4 p.m.
games.v: Comeback of the year from the team that collects them. The Yinzers have now blown two 45-point leads. Frame it.

awards.p: Most points by any starter in the league, and he's started every single week. Josh Allen (256.0, Diddys Oilers) and Jahmyr Gibbs (253.4, LibertyBiberty) are close behind, but neither carried their whole team on their back quite like this.

awards.who: Nakobe Dean · I Can’t Quit Tuten · 187.3
awards.p: The highest-scoring IDP starter in the league, 18.7 a game. The site's new defensive values have him as only the fifth-most valuable linebacker, because he's 25 and his last season was 11.9 a game. Production says MVP; the spreadsheet says prove it again next year.
The best single-game score by a starter, Week 8. Drake Maye's 47.46 for Upper Deckers in Week 5 is second, and is also the only thing Upper Deckers have to put on the fridge this season.
The most in the league, by a lot. The crown jewel: Devin Lloyd's 56.9 in Week 2, the highest score by any player all season, scored from the bench. Truly a museum-quality mistake.
Week 10 against Carson City Yinzers. LibertyBiberty's third win after trailing by 45 or more. At this point, leading LibertyBiberty is just a way to make the loss hurt more.
The fewest points scored against any team in the league. 8-2 with the fifth-most points. Their opponents should be investigated.

Second in points. Third in all-play. Tied for seventh in the standings. Five straight losses from Week 2 to Week 6 while scoring like a contender. The universe owes this team an apology and possibly a cash settlement.

awards.who: I Can’t Quit Tuten · 7 zero-point starters
awards.p: The most in the league, including DJ Moore twice. They are 6-4 anyway, which honestly makes it worse for everyone else.
The only score under 100 all season. Kaleb Johnson scored -0.2 in the lineup. Negative. He owes them points. Josh Cameron chipped in a clean 0.0.

10.note: One game from each week, chosen for what it meant for the season. Game flow shows each team's running score by window: Thursday to Saturday, early Sunday, late Sunday, Sunday night and Monday night, using kickoff times from nflverse. Weekly recaps start with Week 11.

rules.draftOrder: Rookie draft order is based on regular-season record, with last place picking first. Teams that make the playoffs pick in the order they get eliminated, and the champion picks last.
rules.tiebreakNote: Two tiebreaks are the site's assumption, not written rules: teams with the same record are ordered by fewer points for, and the two teams eliminated in the same playoff round pick worse seed first.
rules.other: Anything not listed here follows the Sleeper league settings.
